Fix n, N', L, H_j, H, w and ω. For K ∈ {H_j, H} and I : Fin n → Fin N' put:
- ω_I(y) := ω(y)(e'_{I 0}, …, e'_{I(n−1)}). This is continuous, and |ω_I| ≤ C_ω := sup‖ω‖ < ∞ because ω is continuous with compact support (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm, ‖e'_i‖ = 1).
- Δ_I(K)(u) := det(D(K^{I c})(u)e_b)_{c,b}, where K^i(x) := K(x)_i.

Step 1 (bounds). K^i is L-Lipschitz because |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖. Apply minor_bound with k = r = n and V_b = e_b. Each Δ_I(K) is measurable with |Δ_I(K)| ≤ n!(L·n)^n.

Step 4 (expansion). Apply covector_det_expansion with f = ω(K u) and u_b = DK(u)e_b. This gives n!·Φ_K(u) = Σ_I ω_I(K u)·det((DK(u)e_b)_{I c}). Wherever K is differentiable, the chain rule with the coordinate projection gives D(K^i)(u)e_b = (DK(u)e_b)_i. By Rademacher this holds λ-a.e., so Φ_K = (n!)⁻¹ Σ_I ω_I(K)·Δ_I(K) a.e. Every term w·ω_I(K)·Δ_I(K) is integrable, so ∫ wΦ_K = (n!)⁻¹ Σ_I ∫ w·ω_I(K)·Δ_I(K).

Step 5 (splitting). ∫ w·ω_I(H_j)·Δ_I(H_j) = ∫ w(ω_I(H_j) − ω_I(H))·Δ_I(H_j) + ∫ (w·ω_I(H))·Δ_I(H_j).
- First term → 0 by dominated convergence: the bound is 2C_ω·n!(Ln)^n·|w|, and the integrand tends to 0 pointwise because ω_I is continuous and H_j → H.
- Second term → ∫ (w·ω_I(H))·Δ_I(H) by minor_weak_continuity, with k = r = n, g^j_c := H_j^{I c}, g_c := H^{I c} (L-Lipschitz, converging uniformly since |x_i| ≤ ‖x‖), V_b := e_b and the L¹ weight w·ω_I(H).

Step 7. Sum over the finitely many I and multiply by (n!)⁻¹. Step 2 (n = 0) needs no separate case: there is one I, its determinant is 1, and minor_weak_continuity is trivial for r = 0. Step 6 is minor_weak_continuity together with the leaves below it: lipschitz_minor_ibp, which rests on smooth_minor_ibp, piola_identity and det_covector_exists, and on lipschitz_smooth_approx, mollify_fderiv and mollify_lipschitz; plus weak_star_l1_upgrade and minor_bound.

subproblems.title: Coordinate covector dx^I exists as a continuous determinant covector (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every map I : Fin n → Fin P (no monotonicity or injectivity assumed), there is an n-covector θ on ℝ^P with θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P. Here an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ, and Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). In words, θ(v) is the determinant of the n×n matrix whose (k, j) entry is the I(k)-th coordinate of v_j.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (I : Fin n → Fin P), ∃ θ : Covector (Euclid P) n, ∀ v : Fin n → Euclid P, θ v = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 6(i), which uses d(du_i) = 0; in coordinates this is the Piola identity (sibling piola_identity), whose proof pulls back the constant determinant form constructed here. This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration Submission.cmr_cc_det_covector_exists (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.coordinate_covectors-a1.det_covector_exists-a1, candidate fee01ff8), reused with its identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted proof.

Notation: ℝ^P := Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). For x ∈ ℝ^P and l ∈ Fin P, x(l) (Lean: x l) is the l-th coordinate of x. An n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = (Euclid P) [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ.

1. (Coordinate projection.) Fix P, n and I : Fin n → Fin P. Define p_I : ℝ^P → (Fin n → ℝ) by p_I(x) := (fun k => x(I k)). Since (x + y)(l) = x(l) + y(l) and (c•x)(l) = c·x(l), p_I is ℝ-linear; regard it as p_I : ℝ^P →ₗ[ℝ] (Fin n → ℝ).

2. (Determinant as an alternating map.) Θ := Matrix.detRowAlternating : (Fin n → ℝ) [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ is multilinear and alternating, and Θ(u) = det(Matrix.of u) is the determinant of the matrix whose j-th row is u j. Put θ⁰ := Θ.compLinearMap p_I. By AlternatingMap.compLinearMap_apply, for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P, θ⁰(v) = Θ(fun j => p_I(v j)) = det(Matrix.of fun j k => v j (I k)).

3. (Transpose.) The transpose of Matrix.of fun j k => v j (I k) is Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k), and det Mᵀ = det M (Matrix.det_transpose). Hence θ⁰(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v.

4. (Multiplicative bound.) Fix v and let M := Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k). By the Leibniz formula (Matrix.det_apply), det M = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm(Fin n)} sign(σ)·Π_j v_j(I(σ j)). By the triangle inequality, |sign σ| = 1 (sign σ = ±1), |v_j(I(σ j))| ≤ ‖v_j‖ (a coordinate of a vector of ℝ^P is bounded by its Euclidean norm, PiLp.norm_apply_le) and nonnegativity of all factors (Finset.prod_le_prod₀), |det M| ≤ Σ_σ Π_j ‖v_j‖ = n!·Π_j ‖v_j‖ (card Perm(Fin n) = n!). So ‖θ⁰(v)‖ ≤ n!·Π_j ‖v_j‖.

5. (Continuity and conclusion.) By step 4, AlternatingMap.mkContinuous applies to θ⁰ with constant n!, giving θ := θ⁰.mkContinuous (n!) _ ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n whose underlying function is that of θ⁰. By step 3, θ(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)) for every v : Fin n → ℝ^P, so θ witnesses the claim.

6. (Degenerate cases.) No property of I was used. For n = 0, Perm(Fin 0) has one element and the empty product is 1; θ is the constant map 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.
proof_key_steps: p_I(x) = (x(I k))_k is linear; θ⁰ := Matrix.detRowAlternating ∘ p_I is multilinear alternating with θ⁰(v) = det(v_j(I k))_{j,k}.
Transposing, θ⁰(v) = det(Matrix.of fun k j => v j (I k)).
Leibniz formula and |v_j(l)| ≤ ‖v_j‖ give |θ⁰(v)| ≤ n!·Π‖v_j‖.
AlternatingMap.mkContinuous turns θ⁰ into the required continuous alternating map θ.

subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of a k-covector: k!·f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·det(u_b(I_c)) (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let N', k ∈ ℕ, f a k-covector on ℝ^{N'} (f ∈ Covector (Euclid N') k: a continuous alternating k-linear map (ℝ^{N'})^k → ℝ, ℝ^{N'} = Euclid N') and u = (u_0, …, u_{k−1}) ∈ (ℝ^{N'})^k. Write e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N') for the standard basis of ℝ^{N'} and z(i) for the i-th coordinate of z ∈ ℝ^{N'}. Then k!·f(u) = Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin N'} f(e'_{I(0)}, …, e'_{I(k−1)})·det(M_I), where the sum runs over all maps I (no monotonicity or injectivity) and M_I is the k×k matrix with entry u_b(I(c)) in row c and column b (Lean: Matrix.of fun c b => u b (I c)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N' k : ℕ) (f : Covector (Euclid N') k) (u : Fin k → Euclid N'), (k.factorial : ℝ) * f u = ∑ I : Fin k → Fin N', f (fun c => EuclideanSpace.single (I c) (1 : ℝ)) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun c b => u b (I c))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 (expansion in minors, ω(y)(z_1, …, z_n) = Σ_J ω_J(y)·det[(z_b)_{J(a)}]_{a,b} over strictly increasing J), stated pointwise for one covector f and summed over all index maps I instead of the strictly increasing ones; each strictly increasing J then occurs k! times (as J∘σ), which produces the factor k!. The parent uses it with f = ω(K(u)) and u_b = DK(u)e_b. This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration Submission.dor_lmb_fcd_jwc_covector_det_expansion (candidate 2c87728a), reused with its identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted proof.

Notation. ℝ^{N'} = Euclid N'; e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin N'); z(i) (Lean z i) is the i-th coordinate of z ∈ ℝ^{N'}. For I : Fin k → Fin N' put e'_I := (e'_{I(0)}, …, e'_{I(k−1)}) and let M_I be the k×k matrix with (M_I)_{c,b} = u_b(I(c)).

1. (Basis expansion.) Every z ∈ ℝ^{N'} satisfies z = Σ_{i ∈ Fin N'} z(i)·e'_i (the standard basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun has the coordinates as its repr; Basis.sum_repr). In particular u_b = Σ_i u_b(i)·e'_i for every b.

2. (Multilinear expansion.) f is multilinear, so (MultilinearMap.map_sum) f(u) = Σ_{J : Fin k → Fin N'} f(u_0(J 0)·e'_{J 0}, …, u_{k−1}(J(k−1))·e'_{J(k−1)}), and pulling out the scalars (MultilinearMap.map_smul_univ) each summand equals (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J). Hence f(u) = Σ_J (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J).

3. (Reindexing by a permutation.) Fix σ ∈ Perm(Fin k). The map I ↦ I ∘ σ is a bijection of the finite set of maps Fin k → Fin N' (inverse J ↦ J ∘ σ⁻¹). Substituting J = I ∘ σ in step 2: f(u) = Σ_I (Π_b u_b(I(σ b)))·f(e'_{I(σ 0)}, …, e'_{I(σ(k−1))}).

4. (Alternation.) The family (e'_{I(σ b)})_b is e'_I composed with σ, and an alternating map satisfies f(v ∘ σ) = sign(σ)·f(v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Hence, for every σ, f(u) = Σ_I sign(σ)·(Π_b u_b(I(σ b)))·f(e'_I).

5. (Averaging.) Perm(Fin k) has k! elements (Fintype.card_perm). Summing step 4 over all σ and exchanging the two finite sums: k!·f(u) = Σ_σ f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b u_b(I(σ b)).

6. (Leibniz formula.) By Matrix.det_apply, det M_I = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b (M_I)_{σ(b), b} = Σ_σ sign(σ)·Π_b u_b(I(σ b)). Substituting into step 5 gives k!·f(u) = Σ_I f(e'_I)·det M_I, the claim.

7. (Degenerate cases.) Steps 1–6 use neither k ≥ 1 nor N' ≥ 1. For k = 0 there is exactly one I (the empty map), 0! = 1, the empty determinant is 1 and f(e'_I) = f(u) (both arguments are the empty family). For N' = 0 < k the right side is an empty sum and step 2 gives f(u) = 0.
proof_key_steps: Expand each u_b in the standard basis and use multilinearity: f(u) = Σ_J (Π_b u_b(J b))·f(e'_J).
For each permutation σ reindex J = I ∘ σ and use alternation f(v ∘ σ) = sign(σ) f(v).
Average over the k! permutations and exchange the finite sums.
Recognize Σ_σ sign(σ) Π_b u_b(I(σ b)) as det(u_b(I_c))_{c,b} by the Leibniz formula.

subproblems.title: Averaging against a normalized nonnegative kernel preserves the Lipschitz constant (reused accepted declaration)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, K ≥ 0 (K ∈ ℝ≥0) and ψ, g : ℝ^P → ℝ, where ℝ^P = Euclid P carries Lebesgue measure λ. Suppose ψ is continuous, has compact support, ψ(x) ≥ 0 for every x and ∫ ψ dλ = 1, and g is K-Lipschitz. Then the function x ↦ ∫ ψ(y)·g(x − y) dλ(y) is K-Lipschitz on ℝ^P.

Source: parent proof step 6(i), '|D(h∗ϕ_δ)| ≤ Lip(h)': averaging a Lipschitz function against a nonnegative kernel of integral 1 does not increase its Lipschitz constant (folklore; e.g. Lemma 17 of arXiv:2412.04899). This child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration Submission.cmcs_ls_mollify_lipschitz (candidate 52b9c39c), reused with its identical frozen type; the proof below is its accepted proof.

Notation: λ = volume, Lebesgue measure on Euclid P; ∫ means ∫ … ∂λ; G(x) := ∫ ψ(y)·g(x − y) dλ(y).

1. (Integrability.) g is continuous, being Lipschitz. Fix x. The function h_x(y) := ψ(y)·g(x − y) is continuous, and if h_x(y) ≠ 0 then ψ(y) ≠ 0, so support h_x ⊆ support ψ and h_x has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mul_right). Hence h_x is integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). By the same lemma ψ is integrable, hence so is y ↦ ψ(y)·C for every constant C (Integrable.mul_const).

2. (Difference as one integral.) For x, x' ∈ Euclid P, by step 1 and linearity (integral_sub), G(x) − G(x') = ∫ (ψ(y)·g(x − y) − ψ(y)·g(x' − y)) dλ(y).

3. (Pointwise bound.) For every y: |ψ(y)·g(x − y) − ψ(y)·g(x' − y)| = ψ(y)·|g(x − y) − g(x' − y)| (ψ(y) ≥ 0) ≤ ψ(y)·K·dist(x − y, x' − y) (g is K-Lipschitz) = ψ(y)·K·dist(x, x') (dist_sub_right).

4. (Integration of the bound.) The majorant y ↦ ψ(y)·(K·dist(x, x')) is integrable by step 1, so by step 3 and norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, |G(x) − G(x')| ≤ ∫ ψ(y)·(K·dist(x, x')) dλ(y) = (∫ ψ dλ)·K·dist(x, x') = K·dist(x, x') (integral_mul_const and ∫ ψ = 1).

5. (Conclusion.) dist(G(x), G(x')) ≤ K·dist(x, x') for all x, x', i.e. G = (fun x => ∫ y, ψ y * g (x - y)) is K-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
proof_key_steps: For each x, y ↦ ψ(y)·g(x − y) is continuous with support inside support ψ, hence integrable.
Pointwise |ψ(y)(g(x − y) − g(x' − y))| ≤ ψ(y)·K·dist(x, x').
Integrating with ∫ψ = 1 gives |G(x) − G(x')| ≤ K·dist(x, x').

Then for all x, v ∈ ℝᵏ, Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt, where D = fderiv ℝ (Df(z) is the zero map where f is not differentiable).

D(h∗ϕ_δ) = (Dh)∗ϕ_δ (the a.e. derivative of a Lipschitz function is its weak derivative, Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq)', for one L-Lipschitz function f and an arbitrary C¹ compactly supported kernel ρ. Notation: λ = Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝᵏ = Euclid k; D = fderiv ℝ; ∂_w F(s) := lineDeriv ℝ F s w, the derivative of t ↦ F(s + t·w) at t = 0 (0 if it does not exist); f_ρ(y) := ∫ ρ(t)·f(y − t) dt.

1. (Convolution.) f_ρ is the convolution ρ ⋆ f with the multiplication pairing, i.e. f_ρ = convolution ρ f (lsmul ℝ ℝ) λ (convolution_def: (ρ ⋆ f)(y) = ∫ ρ(t)·f(y − t) dt).

2. (Differentiation under the integral.) ρ is C¹ with compact support and f is continuous (being Lipschitz), hence locally integrable. Therefore ρ ⋆ f has at every x the derivative (Dρ ⋆ f)(x) = ∫ f(x − t)·Dρ(t) dt, a Bochner integral of continuous linear maps (HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_left). This integrand is integrable: Dρ is continuous (ρ is C¹) with compact support and f is locally integrable (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left). Evaluation at v is continuous linear and commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_apply), so Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ Dρ(t)v·f(x − t) dt.

3. (Change of variables.) λ is invariant under s ↦ x − s (integral_sub_left_eq_self), so ∫ Dρ(t)v·f(x − t) dt = ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds and ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds. It remains to show ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds.

4. (Reflected kernel.) Let h(s) := ρ(x − s). h is C¹ (ρ composed with an affine map) and has compact support (its support is the image of the support of ρ under the homeomorphism s ↦ x − s; HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph). A C¹ function with compact support is Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport). By the chain rule Dh(s) = −Dρ(x − s), so ∂_{−v}h(s) = Dh(s)(−v) = Dρ(x − s)v for every s (h is differentiable, DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv).

5. (Integration by parts for Lipschitz functions.) For the L-Lipschitz f and the Lipschitz, compactly supported h, LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq gives ∫ ∂_v f(s)·h(s) ds = ∫ ∂_{−v}h(s)·f(s) ds. By step 4 the right side equals ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds.

6. (Rademacher.) f is differentiable at λ-a.e. s (LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), and at such s, ∂_v f(s) = Df(s)v (DifferentiableAt.lineDeriv_eq_fderiv). Hence ∫ ∂_v f(s)·h(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds (integral_congr_ae).

7. (Conclusion.) Steps 5 and 6 give ∫ Dρ(x − s)v·f(s) ds = ∫ ρ(x − s)·Df(s)v ds, which by steps 2 and 3 is the claim Df_ρ(x)v = ∫ ρ(t)·Df(x − t)v dt.

1. (Approximation.) 2. (Smooth identity.) For every n the g^n_c are C^∞, hence C², and ψ is C¹ with compact support, so the sibling smooth_minor_ibp gives ∫ ψ·det A^n = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^n_0·M^n_b.

3. (Pointwise convergence.) For x ∉ N and all c, b: Dg^n_c(x)V_b → Dg_c(x)V_b (evaluation at V_b is a continuous linear map on the space of linear maps). Matrices converge entrywise and the determinant is continuous (Continuous.matrix_det), so det A^n(x) → det A(x) and M^n_b(x) → M_b(x). Moreover g^n_0(x) → g_0(x) for every x (uniform convergence).

4. (Bounds and measurability.) All g^n_c are L-Lipschitz, so by the sibling minor_bound, det A^n and M^n_b are measurable with |det A^n(x)| ≤ B and |M^n_b(x)| ≤ B_b for all n and x. ψ and ∂_{V_b}ψ are continuous with compact support (Dψ is continuous since ψ is C¹, and it vanishes outside the support of ψ), hence integrable; g^n_0 and g_0 are continuous.

5. (Left side.) |ψ·det A^n| ≤ B·|ψ|, an integrable function independent of n, and ψ·det A^n → ψ·det A outside N by step 3. By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), ∫ ψ·det A^n → ∫ ψ·det A.

6. (Right side.) By uniform convergence there is n_0 with |g^n_0(x) − g_0(x)| ≤ 1 for all x and all n ≥ n_0, hence |g^n_0(x)| ≤ |g_0(x)| + 1. Dominated convergence with a bound valid for all large n (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) gives ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g^n_0·M^n_b → ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b for each b, so the right side of step 2 converges to −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b (finite sums and constant multiples of convergent sequences converge).

7. (Conclusion.) The two sides of step 2 agree for every n; by uniqueness of limits in ℝ (tendsto_nhds_unique) the limits of steps 5 and 6 agree, which is the claimed identity ∫ ψ·det A = −Σ_b (−1)^b ∫ ∂_{V_b}ψ·g_0·M_b.
